77.01.additionalInfo: For additional information, see 77.02 Zheng Zong. Carpal Tunnel Syndrome (Treatment Guide): When treating Carpal Tunnel Syndrome, the foot area is highly effective for addressing conditions of the hand. There is an important principle in acupuncture regarding the use of corresponding influence zones. In the carpal tunnel area, there are two points in Master Tung's acupuncture— Mu Guan and Gu Guan—that affect the foot and heel area. Therefore, points on the foot can be used to influence the hand. The area where the Achilles tendon connects to the heel corresponds to the palmar side of the wrist. For this reason, 77.01 Zheng Jin is an important point for treating Carpal Tunnel Syndrome. I also add 77.02 Zheng Zong. An additional advantage of using these two points is that Carpal Tunnel Syndrome often involves the neck as well. These two points are important points that influence the neck. In addition to the points recommended in the indication search, the following points from the 14 main channels can be added: Ki-3 Taixi, BI-60 Kunlun, Sp-5 Shangqiu, Gb-40 Qiuxu. Needle two needles at St-41 Jiexi—one directed toward Gb-40 Qiuxu, and the other toward Sp-5 Shangqiu. From the perspective of Master Tung's channels, the main channel involved is the Heart channel, which passes through the center of the forearm—such as the points Xin Ling and 33.04-06 Shou San Huo. I also use 33.04—06 Shou San Huo, as well as Tong Ling, located on the Heart channel in the thigh, and two points beside it: 88.10 Tong Wei, and a corresponding point on the Lung channel line, along the same axis as 88.17-19 Si Ma. All of these points are needled on the contralateral side—opposite to the affected hand. Point Name Zhéng — straight, precise, to correct, principal, principle. Jin [5] - tendons and ligaments. The point's name, "Straighten Tendons," suggests its ability to influence the muscles and tendons supporting the spine. For additional information, see 77.03 Zheng Shi.

77.03.additionalInfo: 77.01-03 Zheng Jin/Zong/Shi are sometimes needled using the Dao Ma technique to treat spine and brain disorders. 77.01-02 Zheng Jin/Zong has a greater influence on the spine and brain, while 77.03 Zheng Shi has a greater effect on the upper back and shoulder area. Cases of Master Tung Neck and upper back pain: Needling 77.01-03 Zheng Jin/Zong/Shi. Scapula pain: Needling 77.01-03 Zheng Jin/Zong/Shi. Point Name Zhéng - straight, precise, to correct, principal, principle. Shi [f] — scholar, member of the senior ministerial class, bachelor's degree holder, respectable, soldier, officer, sub-inspector, specialist worker. The character Shi signifies management. In Chapter 8 of the Su Wen, the lungs are described as responsible for managing the state (prime minister). The point's name suggests its connection to the lungs, affecting the spine in the upper back area. The names of the three points, 77.01 Zheng Jin (Straighten Tendons), 77.02 Zheng Zong (Straighten Ancestors), and 77.03 Zheng Shi (Straighten Scholar), hint at a Taoist concept of losing our center. Symbolically, the spine represents the center. The character Zhéng means to correct, to straighten: correcting the tendons that support the spine (77.01 Zheng Jin), correcting our connection to the ancestors (77.02 Zheng Zong), and correcting the management of life so that we can return to being balanced at the center (77.03 Zheng Shi).

77.05-07.additionalInfo: Typically, 77.05 Yi Zhong, 77.06 Er Zhong, and 77.07 San Zhong are needled together using the Dao Ma technique, then called San Zhong [ E ] (Three Weights). They can Typically, 77.05 Yi Zhong, 77.06 Er Zhong, and 77.07 San Zhong are needled together using the Dao Ma technique, then called San Zhong [ E ] (Three Weights). They can eliminate accumulations and clear stagnation of Qi and blood. The Three Weights are primary points for treating the spleen, especially in cases of dampness formation. The spleen is associated with the creation of dampness; therefore, the main innervation of these points is of the spleen. The source of dampness accumulation does not have to be only from excess conditions but can also arise from Qi deficiency. dampness accumulation can cause Qi to stagnate, Which explains Why these points also have innervation for the sub-branch of the lungs (the lungs control Qi). Additionally, Qi stagnation can lead to blood stagnation, which is why these points also have innervation for the sub-branch of the heart (the heart controls blood). It is interesting to note that the location of the Three Weights parallels the Four Flowers' lower points, 77.08, 09, 11 Si Hua. The Four Flowers strengthen the spleen, and at the lower part of this group of points, we find 77.11 Si Hua Xia and 77.12 Fu Chang, two important points for treating intestinal diseases. The Three Weights are important for treating disorders in the neck area, such as throat, tonsil, and thyroid issues, as well as muscle pain on the side of the body. These points significantly influence the brain, making them primary points for treating brain cancer. 77.05-07 San Zhong and 77.27 Wai San Guan have similar functions. Both groups soften swellings and open Qi stagnation, enabling them to treat tumors, but each has a different mechanism of action. The Three Weights treat swelling and stagnation arising from spleen disorders, heart (blood stagnation), and lung diseases (Qi stagnation or deficiency). In contrast, the Three Outer Gates innervate the lungs, making them more suitable for Qi deficiency or stagnation conditions. Their range of action is more limited. Hu wen Zhi 11.14 Zhi San Zhong (Three Weights of the Finger) is more suitable for chest disorders, whereas 77.05-07 San Zhong is more suitable for brain tumors. For treating breast disorders, you can needle 77.05-07 San Zhong together with Shuang Long (77). Lai Jing-Xiong These are important points that Master Tung used for patients after a stroke. The points can open Qi and blood stagnation in the brain. Master Tung used this group of points to treat early stages of breast, esophageal, and tongue cancer, achieving good results. The Three Weights and 88.01-03 Tong Guan/Shan/Tian can treat hyperthyroidism. 77.08.additionalInfo: The point's name reflects the spleen's transformation and transportation of postnatal Qi. The point's innervation (branch of the lungs and heart) reflects the result of this action: the creation of Qi (lungs) and blood (heart). 77.08 Si Hua Shang influences the mechanism of transforming and transporting the Ying Qi. It affects the upper part of the digestive system (the source of postnatal Qi), mainly including the mouth, teeth, and stomach. The point's ability to regulate the creation of postnatal Qi through digestion affects the lungs and heart. The point does not act directly on the lungs and heart but through the earth (spleen and stomach). The spleen and stomach are responsible for transforming the Gu Qi and transporting it to the upper burner. In the lungs, it becomes the protective Qi, and in the heart, it becomes blood. When cholera is mentioned, it refers not only to the disease but also to vomiting and diarrhea. For more additional information, see 77.11 Si Hua Xia. Bloodletting — Mouth and Teeth Area The upper part of the calf, from the anterior to the lateral area, reflects the mouth and teeth. The bloodletting of the connecting channels in this area can treat aphthae, mouth tumors, herpes on the lips, toothache, and gum problems. Points located in this area include 77.08 Si Hua Shang, 77.15-16 Shang/Xia Chun, and 77.22-23 Ce/Xia San Li. Point Name Point Name Si - four. Huä [it] — flower. Shång [El — upper. Huä [7E] - flower. Shång [YI — upper. In the Yellow River Map, the number four represents metal. The lungs belong to the metal element, so the point's name suggests its influence on the lungs. The flower in the name symbolizes summer, and summer is associated with the fire phase (heart). Therefore, the point's name also indicates its effect on the heart. There is also a hidden meaning in the name. At the top of the character Huä [ (flower), there is the radical cäo [ (grass), and below it is the character Huå (to transform). The spleen transforms, so the Huä - flower. point's name suggests its connection with the earth (spleen). Flowers grow from the earth. The point's name suggests its mechanism of action: the transformation of Gu qi by the spleen and its transportation to the upper burner, the lungs, and the heart to generate protective qi and blood. The "Upper" in the name indicates that this is the uppermost point among the Four Flowers (Si Hua), affecting the upper part of the digestive system. Shång — upper.

77.11.additionalInfo: 77.08 Si Hua Shang, 77.09 Si Hua Zhong, and 77.11 Si Hua Xia are often needled together using the Dao Ma technique. This combination is called the Four Flowers (Si Hua [ gg J). The flower in the point's name symbolizes summer. Summer is associated with the fire phase (heart), so the points' names suggest their influence on the heart. However, there is also a hidden meaning in the name; at the bottom of the character, Hua (flower), appears the radical Hua [ l, which means to transform. In Chinese medicine, the spleen is responsible for transformation, so the name of the points suggests the influence of the Four Flowers on the spleen (pancreas), especially the role of the spleen in digestion. Therefore, the Four Flowers are also used for digestive disorders. The Four Flowers is an important combination that can strengthen postnatal Qi. The spleen (pancreas) transforms food that rises to the upper burner to support the heart and lungs. In the lungs, it becomes the protective Qi, and in the heart, it becomes blood. Therefore, the Four Flowers points also impact the heart and lungs. The Four Flowers combination strengthens all aspects of postnatal Qi (nutritive Qi, protective Qi, and blood) by regulating the digestive system. The Four Flowers can treat gynecological disorders when Qi and blood deficiency are present for conditions such as amenorrhea, dysmenorrhea, and irregular menstruation. 77.11 Si Hua Xia and 77.12 Fu Chang are essential points for treating intestinal diseases, and they are often needled together using the Dao Ma technique. Differential Diagnosis of the Four Flowers 77.08 Si Hua Shang treats the mouth, teeth, and stomach. 77.08 Si Hua Shang and 77.09 Si Hua Zhong treat the lungs and heart. 77.11 Si Hua Xia and 77.12 Fu Chang treat the intestines. Lee Kuo Cheng If 77.08, 09, II Si Hua are needled on the right side, the points also influence the liver, lungs, spleen, and heart. Therefore, combining Si Hua on the right side with 88.09, IO, II Tong Shen/Wei/Bei on the left side, which are points influencing the kidneys, strengthens all five solid organs. 77.08, 09, II Si Hua can treat female and thyroid reproductive systems disorders. Lai Jing-Xiong 77.11 Si Hua Xia and 77.12 Fu Chang can treat sciatica due to a herniated disc. Case — Master Tung A patient with left shoulder pain. Master Tung needled on the right side 77.11 Si Hua Xia, and two more points 1 cun above and below 77.11 Si Hua Xia. Bloodletting — Heart Area The Four Flowers are located in the anterior bloodletting area of the calf, known as the heart area. If connecting channels exist in the area, they can be bled to treat heart diseases: chest operation, palpitations, angina pectoris, endocarditis (inflammation of the inner heart), arrhythmias, valve disorders, and high blood lipid levels (hyperlipidemia). Additionally, bloodletting in the area can treat stomach and intestinal diseases, lung diseases, pneumonia, eye diseases, and headaches. Point Name Si - four. Huä [lü - flower. Xiå [F] — lower. The character "lower" in the point's name suggests it is the lowest point among the Four Flowers (Si Hua). Xiå [T] — lower. For additional information about the point's name, see 77.08 Si Hua Shang.

The Three Lower Emperors can increase blood flow during menstruation, so their use should be considered carefully during this time. They are typically used before and after menstruation. Two main Dao Ma groups affect the kidneys: the Three Lower Emperors (77.17, 19, 21 Xia San Huang) and 88.09, 10, 11 Tong Shen/Wei/Bei. The main difference is that the Three Lower Emperors are contraindicated during pregnancy, whereas 88.09, IO, II Tong Shen/Wei/Bei can prevent miscarriage. For more information on the differences between these two groups, see 88.11 Tong Bei. Additionally, 77.17, 19, 21 Xia San Huang are often combined with 88.12-14 Shang San Huang to treat kidney and liver diseases. Chuan Min Wang Many acupuncturists believe that the Three Lower Emperors should be needled bilaterally. This is not the correct method. To determine where to needle, you should palpate the entire line of the Three Lower Emperors and look for areas where you find nodules or a cord-like feeling in the tissue. You should also observe the patient's body language during palpation. Needling is based on these findings. Sometimes, one needle is used, sometimes two, and sometimes three. This technique applies to all point groups, not just the Three Lower Emperors. The bloodletting of the connecting channels in the area can treat nephritis, cystitis, urethritis, irregular menstruation, dysmenorrhea, uterine inflammation, ovarian inflammation, lower back pain due to kidney deficiency, stomach pressure, and hyperacidity. Point Name Rén [Al - person, human. Huång [Q] - emperor. The character "Human" in the point's name indicates that it is the lowest point among the three Emperor points (Huang). There are three points with the character "emperor" in their names: 77.17 Tian Huang (Emperor of the Heaven), 77.19 Di Huang (Emperor of the Earth), and 77.21 Ren Huang (Emperor of the Human). There are two ways to arrange Heaven, Earth, and Human. The first is Heaven-person-Earth, with the Human being between Heaven and Earth. The second arrangement, which is more related to Taoism, is Heaven-Earth-Human. Chapter 25 of the Dao De Jing is written: "Man follows the Earth, the Earth follows the Heaven, the Heaven follows the Dao, and the Dao follows nature." Master Tung used the second arrangement. The upper point is 77.17 Tian Huang (Emperor of the Heaven), the middle point is 77.19 Di Huang (Emperor of the Earth), and the lower point is 77.21 Ren Huang (Emperor of the Human). Master Tung's choice of the second arrangement is another example of his connection with Taoism. Huång [fl — emperor.

77.24.additionalInfo: 77.24 Zu Qian Jin is typically used with 77.25 Zu Wu Jin as a Dao Ma group. 77.24-25 Zu Qian/Wu Jin influences the throat and can be used for many throat disorders, including throat infections, tonsillitis, and even conditions where something feels stuck in the throat, such as a fishbone. This can also be a subjective feeling of something stuck in the throat for emotional reasons (Globus hystericus). The points are associated with metal, so they can also treat throat dryness that leads to coughing. These points also affect the intestines and can treat intestinal inflammations. They are very effective for shoulder and arm movement disorders. Lai Jin Xiong Zu Qian Jin and Zu Wu Jin can treat pain in the posterior aspect of the shoulder joint. Needling Zu Qian Jin and Zu Wu Jin is effective for pain that forms a connecting line across the shoulder, the back of the head, and the temples. Bloodletting Area — Lungs The lateral side of the calf reflects the lungs in the area of points 77.24-25 Zu Qian/Wu Jin and 77.27 Wai San Guan. The bloodletting of the connecting channels in this area can treat pneumonia, asthma, bronchitis, emphysema, middle back pain, shoulder pain, endocarditis (inflammation of the heart lining), pericarditis (inflammation of the heart's outer lining), arrhythmias, hypertension, throat infections, facial paralysis, and acne. There are three groups of points with the name "Thousand/Five Metal": 11.08 Zhi Wu Qian Jin, 33.08-09 Shou Qian/Wu Jin (Hand Thousand/Five Metal), and 77.24-25 Zu Qian/Wu Zü [E] — leg. Qian Jin [T±] — Thousand Gold: In classical Chinese culture, "Thousand Gold" signifies immense, priceless value — something beyond ordinary measure. The Tang dynasty physician-sage Sun Simiao [ -fh ] named his great clinical masterwork precisely this: Essential Formulas Worth a Thousand Gold [ fM + fi l, explaining in his preface that a human life surpasses a thousand gold in worth, and a single formula that saves it surpasses even that. In Chinese medicine, Qian Jin carries this dual weight — the priceless value of a life, and the remedy that rescues it at the critical moment. Zü [RI — leg. Clinically, the name reflects the point's outstanding capacity to resolve acute, distressing crises instantly — severe abdominal pain from acute enteritis or appendicitis, or the physical emergency of a fish bone lodged in the throat. Like the formula worth a thousand gold, this point earns its name when all else fails and the situation cannot wait. Zü [R] — leg. Jin [ft] — metal. Qian Jin [fff] — Thousand Gold:

77.25.additionalInfo: For additional information, see 77.24 Zu Qian Jin. Point Name Zü [El — leg. Wü - five. Wü [E] - five. Jin [+] — metal. Wu Jin — Five Metals: Zü [RI — leg. Where Qian Jin names the singular, priceless gold, Wu Jin names the full spectrum — the five classical metals of ancient China: Gold [ l, Silver [ l, Copper [ l, Iron [ l, and Tin Together they represent the complete range of what metal can do: not one concentrated peak of value, but the entire functional breadth of Metal's nature. In Five Phase terms, Metal governs the Lung and Large Intestine, the skin and defensive Wei Qi layer, and the body's capacity to descend, disperse, and release. Five Metals Jin [ft] — metal. suggests this point activates that full range — and clinically this is precisely what we see. The pair 77.24 and 77.25 addresses both Metal organ systems directly: throat and respiratory disorders on the Lung side, and intestinal disorders on the Large Intestine side. The throat emergency of a fish bone lodged in the throat, acute respiratory distress, and the abdominal crisis of acute enteritis or appendicitis — all fall within Metal's domain, and all respond to these points. Zü [R] — leg. Clinically, 77.25 is almost never used alone — it works as a pair with 77.24 Zu Qian Jin, and the naming carries that logic perfectly. Thousand Gold for the acute rescue, Five Metals for the comprehensive metallic action. Together they cover the full territory that neither could reach alone.

77.26.additionalInfo: The 7126 Qi Hu point serves as a specialized distal representation of the bony structures and linings of the upper thoracic cage and neck. The reaction area of these points includes the ribs and sternum. This group demonstrates significant distal resonance, effectively addressing structural skeletal pain such as scapular, clavicular, and sternal pain, as well as localized swelling. This point is specifically indicated for the alleviation of pleurisy, defined as inflammation of the lung linings. The 77.26 Qi Hu point is particularly effective for acute neck muscle sprains and is considered a primary option for rapid restoration of neck mobility. It may be combined with the BI-60 Kun Lun point. These points may be combined in the management of cervical herniated disc cases that present with radiating pain to the arms. Bloodletting Area — Chest The area of points 77.26 Qi Hu reflects the chest. The bloodletting of the connecting channels in this area can treat shoulder pain, pain and swelling of the clavicle, rib area pain, and ankle sprains. 77.27.additionalInfo: Master Tung designated 77.27 Wai San Guan as one of his 72 Unique Needles (Éé?f) due to its potent systemic clearing capabilities. These points are believed to dissolve hard masses, including accumulations of Qi, blood, and phlegm. According to Chinese medical theory, tumors, cancers, and swollen lymph nodes (scrofula) are considered manifestations of dense toxic heat, stagnant phlegm, and congealed blood. These points influence the lungs, which are responsible for the descending and diffusing functions in Chinese medicine. As the lungs govern the Qi of the entire body and regulate the skin and mucosal linings, stimulation of these points is thought to facilitate the resolution of physical accumulations, clear heat, and eliminate toxins. Consequently, these points are reported to be effective in treating laryngeal and lung cancers, tonsillitis, and persistent facial acne. Both 77.05-07 San Zhong and 77.27 Wai San Guan exhibit similar therapeutic functions. Each group reduces swelling and alleviates Qi stagnation, contributing to their effectiveness in tumor treatment, although their mechanisms of action differ. San Zhong addresses swelling and stagnation associated with spleen disorders, heart diseases involving blood stagnation, and lung diseases characterized by Qi stagnation or deficiency. In contrast, Wai San Guan, which is associated with the lungs, is more appropriate for cases of Qi deficiency or stagnation, though its therapeutic range is comparatively limited. In the treatment of cancerous tumors, both groups may be combined with additional points selected according to the tumor's anatomical location. For instance, in cases of stomach cancer, bloodletting in the corresponding leg region and needling of 77.22-23 ce/Xia san Li, 77.08 Si Hua Shang, 66.05 Men Jin, 77.05-07 san Zhong, and 77.27 wai san Guan are considered effective. 77.27 Wai San Guan is also indicated for the treatment of shoulder disorders, particularly when radiating pain extends along the arm. Hu wen Zi For the treatment of cervical tumors and cancer, combining 77.27 Wai San Guan with 11.24 Fuke (selecting any two points from the Fuke group) is reported to be particularly effective. In the management of scrofula and malignant tumors, the combination of 77.27 Wai San Guan with 77.05-07 San Zhong, 88.25 Jiu Li, and 22.05 Ling Gu points is reported to yield high efficacy, with claimed cure rates exceeding 90%. Lai Jin Xiong Needling this point in conjunction with 77.22 Ce Xia San Li reportedly produces excellent outcomes in the treatment of toothache. Utilizing this point in combination with 77.22 Ce Xia San Li is also reported to be effective in the treatment of migraine headaches. Point Name Wåi [5b] - external. Sän [E] — three. Guän [Nd] — gate. Wai [5b] refers to the Exterior or lateral aspect, indicating the physical location of the point group on the lateral side of the lower leg. Master Tung's emphasis on the term 'Exterior' implies the existence of 'Three Inner Gates.' In records of his initial treatment of Cambodian President Lon Nol following a stroke, Master Tung references the use of the Three Inner Gates (Nei San Guan [ 1!51). Although these points were employed on multiple occasions, their precise anatomical locations were not specified. Sän [2] — three. Guän — gate. Guan [ ] translates as Pass or Gateway. In Chinese medicine, a Pass is considered a critical strategic gateway where Qi may become obstructed, but which also allows practitioners to unlock and mobilize deep circulation. The designation of this group as the Three Passes signifies their clinical capacity to address persistent, stagnant blockages that protect the upper body's defensive regions.

ShuangLong.additionalInfo: Double Dragon points are systemic points for treating chest tumors due to their ability to release Qi and Blood stagnation in the chest. In men, the breast is related to the Kidneys and the nipple to the Liver, while in women, the breast is associated with the Stomach and the nipple to the Liver. Due to the point's effect on the nipple, Li Guo Zheng adds Liver branch innervation. In Master Tung's acupuncture, points related to the Lungs affect breast tumors, mainly because the Lungs influence smooth Qi flow in the chest. When Qi stagnation occurs in the chest, and the Lungs' ability to descend Qi is impaired, the phlegm may form over time, leading to masses and tumors in the chest. Chest tumors can also form due to Blood stagnation. The point's name indicates its ability to treat Blood stagnation in the chest. Combine Qi stagnation conditions with 88.17-19 Sima (Lung innervation and Liver sub-branch) and 77.27 Wai San Guan (Lung innervation). Since Sima also has liver innervation, it affects the nipple. For Qi and Blood stagnation conditions, combine with 44 Jian Feng (Lung and Heart sub-branch innervation) and 77.05-07 San Zhong (Spleen, Lung and Heart sub-branch innervation). Hu Wen Zhi The points do not appear in Master Tung's original book. Hu Wen Zhi introduced them. These are essential for treating chest diseases and are two of the 72 Absolute Needles of Tung. For chest diseases, combine with 44 Jian Feng. To improve the effect, bleeding can be applied to the Lung and Heart areas on the back and the Lung and Heart areas on the leg. The character "double" in the point name indicates the points' connection to the Heart and their ability to treat Blood stagnation in the chest. In the Chinese zodiac, the Dragon is associated with the Stomach. In Chinese medicine, the breast is also related to the Stomach. Thus, the points' name indicates their ability to treat Blood stagnation in the chest.
